title: HackKumbh 2026 : Tech For Humanity
description: HackKumbh 2026 | Honouring a Legacy, Innovating the Future Theme — Tech for Humanity: Innovating for Health, Education and Rural Empowerment What would you build to make healthcare easier to access, help students learn with limited connectivity, or solve a problem facing a rural community? HackKumbh 2026 is a national-level hackathon organised by Yeshwantrao Chavan College of Engineering (YCCE), Nagpur. Held in memory of Late Shri Datta Meghe Ji, it invites college students from across India to turn ideas for health, education and rural empowerment into working prototypes. Use AI, IoT, data analytics, robotics or digital platforms where they fit. Start with a specific problem and the people who face it. Then show how your solution could work in practice and be affordable and accessible to the people it serves. Who can participate? Open to college students across India Teams of 2–5 members Round 1 Problem Statements Choose one of the 15 problem statements for your PPT submission. Healthcare — Clinic appointments and queues, personal medical records and prescriptions, medicine and diagnostic price comparison, medication reminders and dose tracking, or multilingual health awareness and symptom guidance. Education — Internship matching and progress tracking, offline learning, peer learning and doubt resolution, an AI tutor based on teacher-approved material, or multilingual learning support. Social Issues — Urban sanitation and waste reporting, rural and semi-urban skills and job matching, digital literacy and fraud awareness for senior citizens, water scarcity and groundwater monitoring, or help finding and applying for government welfare schemes. Download the PPT Round Problem Statements PDF attached below for the full briefs, core features, expected prototypes and PPT guidelines. Read your chosen brief before preparing your submission. Stages and format Stage 1 — Online Idea Submission on Unstop Submit a presentation outlining the problem, who it affects, your proposed solution, how you plan to build it and its expected impact. Submissions will be reviewed for the problem addressed, the proposed solution, technical approach, feasibility and expected impact. The top 50 teams will advance to the on-campus finale. Stage 2 — 24-Hour On-Campus Build Shortlisted teams will develop a working prototype at YCCE, Nagpur. Teams will receive feedback during mentoring and review sessions and use it to refine their prototypes before the final submission. Stage 3 — Live Demo and Final Presentation Present your prototype to the jury. Show what it does, explain how it addresses the problem and describe what it would take to put it into use. Proposed prizes and recognition Winner — ₹1,00,000 First runner-up — ₹75,000 Second runner-up — ₹50,000 Total cash prize pool — ₹2,25,000 Five teams may receive special mentions, and two promising startup ideas may be considered for incubation or mentoring. Event details Proposed finale dates — 18–19 December 2026 Venue — Yeshwantrao Chavan College of Engineering (YCCE), Nagpur Proposed finale fee — ₹2,000 per shortlisted team Form your team, pick a problem worth solving and submit your idea on Unstop.

title: ELU Build
description: About ELUBuild ELUBuild is the flagship solo product-building challenge by EduLinkUp . Over the course of the buildathon, individual builders pitch innovative software ideas, and once approved, build, document, and ship real-world SaaS applications from the ground up. The mission of ELUBuild is to discover and empower solo builders to create sustainable, user-ready digital products. Exceptional projects will be selected for integration into the ELU Store platform, with opportunities for direct deployment, hosting, and potential publishing on the Google Play Store on behalf of EduLinkUp. The Complete Event Flow ELUBuild runs across clear, structured phases: Registration & Track Exploration: Register via the EduLinkUp mobile app. Review the announced tracks and loose problem statement suggestions provided by EduLinkUp. These serve as inspiration-participants are completely free to think beyond these suggestions and tackle any authentic, high-impact problem within the domain. Use this phase to brainstorm, validate needs, and prepare your pitch before the idea portal opens. Idea Submission Phase: When the idea window opens, submit your idea proposal (project name, problem statement, target users, proposed solution, anticipated tech stack, solo buildability feasibility, and an explanatory video link). You can submit anytime while the window is active. Continuous Review & Approval: The EduLinkUp team reviews submissions on a rolling basis. Ideas can be approved at any time while the window is open. Share Your Vision: Once your idea is approved, you can (and are encouraged to) publish your explanatory pitch video on social media. Social Media Engagement Leaderboard (Active in Idea & Build Phases): A dedicated engagement leaderboard tracks reach, quality, and engagement of participants' social media posts across both the Idea Phase and the Building Phase . Compelling explanations, progress updates, and demos that resonate with the community rank higher. Idea Phase Closure, Review & Stage 1 Certification: The idea submission portal closes at 11:59 PM IST on the deadline day. The final review round is completed, and results are officially released to all participants. Stage 1 Certification: All builders whose ideas are approved receive official Stage 1 ELUBuild recognition and advance to the building phase. Building Phase (Next.js + Supabase): Building takes place inside the edulinkup-interns GitHub organisation. Shortlisted builders create their public repository under edulinkup-interns . Mandatory Tech Stack: Projects must be built using Next.js and Supabase , with authentication integrated via EduLinkUp OAuth ( @edulinkup/auth SDK). Detailed step by step instructions/guide of connecting your site with EduLinkUp OAuth will be shared before the building phase. Weekly Social Updates: Builders must share at least one weekly progress update on social media (e.g., #buildinpublic , feature demos, architecture highlights, or lessons learned). Engaging, authentic content helps you climb the Social Leaderboard. Repository Commits & Commit Quality Leaderboard: Steady, consistent development through the build window is tracked on a dedicated Commit Leaderboard . Quality & Consistency Over Raw Volume: Scoring evaluates steady engineering rhythm, meaningful commit messages, and genuine code evolution-not artificial commit spamming or scripts. Manual Audits: Code and repository activity will be regularly inspected manually. Use of commit bots, artificial commit scripts, or bulk dumping pre-existing code on the final day will lead to immediate disqualification . Final Submission & Judging: Submit your GitHub repository (under edulinkup-interns ), a deployed live demo URL, and a comprehensive product walkthrough video. Independent evaluations determine top ranks (Winner / Top 1, Top 3, Top 5, Top 7, and All participants). Event Conclusion, Rewards & ELU Store Integration: Winners and top builders receive trophies, official swags kits, domain vouchers, AI interview vouchers, and certificates. ELU Store Launch: The best app(s) are selected for ecosystem integration into the ELU Store , with maintenance support, live showcase, and potential Google Play Store publication under the EduLinkUp organisation. Participation & Eligibility Solo Builders Only: Participation is strictly individual. No teams, shared accounts, or outsourced engineering. App-Verified Registration: Registration must be completed via the official EduLinkUp Android app. GitHub Requirement: A valid GitHub profile link must be provided. EduLinkUp issues invitations to the edulinkup-interns organization. Ensure you accept the GitHub organization invite before the build window starts. One Idea Per Participant: Each builder may submit one proposal per edition. Ideas can be edited until the submission window closes. Idea Proposal Submission Guidelines Your pitch must address a real-world problem and clearly articulate how it will be delivered solo. Submissions include: Project Name: Clear, brandable name for your product. Problem Statement: Specific, concrete friction point you are solving. Target Users: Exact demographic or professional segment that experiences this problem. Evidence of Need: Why this problem exists and proof that users care. Proposed Solution: Your functional approach and feature roadmap. Anticipated Tech Stack: Confirmation of Next.js, Supabase, and auxiliary APIs/libraries. Solo Buildability Note: Feasibility explanation detailing how the core MVP can be built solo within the build window. Idea Video Link: A public link (YouTube, Loom, Google Drive) explaining your concept clearly in English or Hindi (1-3 minutes). Note: Ideas are reviewed on merit and feasibility. Clearing this stage qualifies you for the Stage 1 Certificate and unlocks the Building Phase. Technical & Building Standards All projects in the building phase must adhere to the following rules: GitHub Organization: All code must live inside a public repository created in the edulinkup-interns GitHub organisation. Repository ownership remains with the organisation. Standard Tech Stack: Frontend & Framework: Next.js (App Router recommended). Backend & Database: Individual Supabase project owned and managed by the participant. Authentication: EduLinkUp OAuth using @edulinkup/auth . Detailed step-by-step instructions and guides for connecting your application with EduLinkUp OAuth will be shared with all shortlisted builders prior to the building phase. Genuine Work Created in Window: All code must be authored during the active build window. Re-submitting existing projects or templates with trivial tweaks is strictly prohibited. Secret Security: Never commit service-role keys, private API secrets, or database passwords to public repositories. Utilise .env.local and environment variables. Permitted Resources: Open-source npm packages, public APIs, and AI coding assistants (e.g., Gemini, Copilot, Cursor) are allowed, provided you understand, customize, and own your codebase. Integrity & Anti-Bot Rule: Commits must reflect authentic engineering progress. Scripted commit bots, fake green-square generators, or plagiarized repos result in immediate disqualification. Final Submission Checklist At the conclusion of the build window, participants submit: Repository Link: Working, clean repository in edulinkup-interns . Live Production URL: A fast, functional deployed application (e.g., on Vercel) that judges and visitors can test directly. Demo & Walkthrough Video: Public video demonstrating the end-to-end user workflow, core features, and product value. Builder Philosophy ELUBuild is not an academic exercise or a mock hackathon. It is a launchpad to build an authentic, lasting software product that people genuinely use. Build independently. Build publicly. Build something worth keeping. A solo product-building competition: pitch an idea, and if it is shortlisted, build and ship it in the build window. Each edition has one fixed track and one winner.

title: Rabinjathon: Prime 1
description: Overview RABINJATHON is a student-led, online-first innovation and project-building event organized by RABINJA SQUAD. The event is designed for participants who want to take an idea beyond a presentation — develop a concept, build a working prototype or demonstrable solution, explain how it works, and present it before a panel of judges. The event will begin in an online format. Depending on the event schedule and feasibility, selected/final-stage activities may be conducted in a hybrid format. Any confirmed hybrid requirements, venue details, or physical participation information will be communicated to eligible participants in advance. Event Approach Participants are expected to develop their own original idea, product, prototype, or solution. There is no single fixed problem statement that every team must solve. Participants may work across different areas such as software, web development, hardware, robotics, open innovation, and other technology-oriented concepts. The focus is on creativity, development, demonstration, communication, and practical thinking. Participants are encouraged to build and demonstrate a functional prototype wherever reasonably possible. Teams should be able to explain what their solution does, how it works, and what problem it is intended to address. Eligibility & Team Format Participation is open to students and eligible learners as specified in the registration requirements. Solo participation is allowed. Teams may consist of 1–4 participants. Inter-college teams are allowed. Participants from different academic specializations/branches may form a team. Team members do not need to belong to the same college, course, or specialization. Each participant should provide accurate information during registration. Participants may be required to provide additional details or proof of eligibility if requested by the organizers. A team can therefore be formed around the idea and skills required for the project rather than being restricted to one institution or specialization. Event Format RABINJATHON: PRIME 1 will progress through multiple stages. The rounds are designed to evaluate not only the idea itself, but also how participants develop, demonstrate, communicate, and defend their solution. Round 1 — Product Introduction / Ad-Style Video Participants will create a short video of approximately 2 minutes introducing their product, project, or solution. The video should be presented in an engaging, attention-grabbing format similar to a professional product advertisement or launch introduction. The video should communicate: Product/project name Product logo or visual identity, where applicable The problem or need being addressed A concise introduction to the solution Key value or purpose of the product Why someone would be interested in the solution An engaging introduction that captures the viewer's attention Participants may use creative storytelling, demonstrations, visuals, mock advertisements, animations, or other suitable presentation techniques. Where a participant uses an officially sponsored/partnered product, service, API, platform, or tool, the relevant sponsor/partner branding may be required to be displayed or acknowledged according to the applicable usage guidelines and permissions. Participants must not imply sponsorship, endorsement, partnership, or affiliation with any company unless such relationship has been officially confirmed and authorized. Detailed Round 1 submission instructions, technical requirements, submission procedure, deadlines, and any applicable branding requirements will be shared with registered participants approximately one week before the round. Round 2 — Project Showcase / Working Explainer Participants progressing to Round 2 will create a video of up to 5 minutes explaining their project in greater depth. This round is intended to demonstrate that the concept is not only an idea, but something that has been developed, prototyped, tested, or otherwise demonstrated to a meaningful extent. Participants should explain: What the project does The problem being addressed How the solution works Major components or technologies involved The current stage of development Prototype/demo functionality How the product could work in a real-world scenario What makes the approach different or useful Think of this round as a behind-the-scenes product showcase — similar to how technology and manufacturing programmes demonstrate a product being developed and prepared, while keeping confidential implementation details or proprietary "secret sauce" private. Participants are NOT required to publicly disclose sensitive intellectual property, confidential algorithms, private credentials, proprietary datasets, or other information they do not wish to reveal. The objective is to provide enough evidence and demonstration to establish that the project has been meaningfully developed. Final Round — Live Pitch & Judge Interaction Finalists will present their ideas/projects before a panel of judges. The final presentation will allow participants to: Present the problem and proposed solution Demonstrate or explain the developed product/prototype Explain the project's working and implementation Discuss practical applications and future possibilities Answer questions from the judging panel Respond to feedback and observations from the judges Judges may ask questions regarding the idea, implementation, technology, feasibility, originality, demonstration, or potential application of the project. Following the interaction, the judging panel will evaluate the submissions according to the applicable judging criteria and may provide suggestions, observations, or feedback to the participants. Timeline Registration Opens: 18 October 2026 Registration Deadline: As specified on the official Unstop opportunity page. Round 1: Scheduled after the registration phase. Detailed submission instructions and the confirmed Round 1 timeline will be communicated to registered participants approximately one week before the round. Round 2: Participants qualifying from Round 1 will receive the Round 2 submission schedule and instructions in advance. Final Round: Finalists will receive the final presentation schedule, format, and participation instructions in advance. Event Mode: Online-first. Hybrid Component: A hybrid component may be introduced for selected/final-stage activities depending on the finalized event plan and feasibility. Any confirmed physical participation requirements will be communicated separately in advance. Participants should regularly check the official Unstop opportunity page and the communication channels provided by the organizers for schedule updates. General Rules Participants must submit their own work and provide accurate information during registration. Plagiarism, fraudulent submissions, impersonation, fabricated results, or misrepresentation of a project's development status may result in disqualification. Teams must have 1–4 members and should ensure that all registered team members are genuine participants. Participants may use publicly available technologies, frameworks, APIs, development tools, AI-assisted tools, libraries, and other legitimate resources unless specifically restricted in the round instructions. If external tools, APIs, datasets, models, or third-party resources are used, participants should disclose their meaningful use where requested by the organizers or judging criteria. Participants must not share passwords, API keys, private credentials, confidential information, or other sensitive data in their submissions. Participants must respect the intellectual property rights, licenses, trademarks, and usage conditions of third-party software, APIs, datasets, media, logos, and other resources. Company, sponsor, partner, or product logos must not be used in a way that falsely suggests endorsement, sponsorship, or official partnership. Any confirmed sponsor/partner branding requirements communicated by the organizers must be followed. Participants are responsible for ensuring that submitted videos, images, music, software, datasets, and other materials can legally be used in their submission. Participants should not disclose confidential or proprietary information that they are not authorized to share. The organizers may request clarification, supporting material, a demonstration, or additional information regarding a submission where necessary for evaluation. Participants must follow the submission format, file requirements, deadlines, and other instructions communicated for each round. Late or incomplete submissions may not be considered unless an exception is explicitly communicated by the organizers. The organizers reserve the right to disqualify submissions that violate the event rules or applicable laws. The judging panel's evaluation will be based on the criteria communicated for the respective stage. Any event updates, schedule changes, additional requirements, or round-specific instructions will be communicated through the official channels used for the event. Important RABINJATHON is organized as a student-led initiative by RABINJA SQUAD. The event is intended to provide participants with an opportunity to build, showcase, communicate, and receive feedback on their ideas and projects. Participants should not assume that participation, selection, judging feedback, sponsorship, partnership, publication, investment, employment, or any other external opportunity is guaranteed unless it is explicitly confirmed by the organizers. Specific round instructions, judging criteria, submission requirements, branding requirements, and timelines may be updated or communicated separately as the event progresses. Participants are encouraged to keep checking the official event page and organizer communications for the latest information. title: The Algo Trading Innovation Challenge
description: About The Algo Trading Innovation Challenge is a national fintech competition by Delta Exchange and Techfest, IIT Bombay, built around a stark fact: SEBI found that 87.7% of individual equity-derivatives traders made net losses in FY26. Teams study Delta Exchange's AlgoHub, its ecosystem of six algorithmic trading features, identify a significant gap that Futures and Options traders face, and design an original, AI-assisted capability that goes beyond what the platform offers today. The top 50 teams turn their ideas into working prototypes at an on-campus hackathon at Techfest, IIT Bombay, Asia's largest science and technology festival. Structure The competition runs in two rounds, with Round 2 as an on-campus hackathon at Techfest, IIT Bombay. Eligibility: Open to all students with a valid ID from their educational institution. Cross-institutional teams are encouraged. Team size: Maximum 4 members per team. The Challenge: Teams select one or two (maximum two) of the six AlgoHub features, Algo Marketplace, Algo Builder, API Copilot, Trading Bot, APIs, or Trade Data, identify a significant product gap or unmet need that F&O traders face within them, and design an innovative, AI-assisted capability that adds meaningful functionality beyond what exists today. Teams may propose an independent innovation per feature or one unified solution covering both. Delta Exchange is already working on natural-language strategy creation, backtesting, and trading intelligence, so teams are encouraged not to build their proposal primarily around those capabilities. Round 1 - Online Submission (Screening) A conceptual round; no working prototype is required and teams do not need to deploy live strategies or trade with real capital. Teams submit a presentation of no more than 6 slides (PPT/PPTX or PDF export) covering: Selected Feature(s) & Product Understanding Problem Identification & Product Gap Proposed AI-Assisted Innovation Real-World Trading Use Case Technical Approach & Feasibility Expected Impact & Value Only the Team Leader may submit. The 50 highest-scoring teams qualify for Round 2; ties at the cutoff are broken by the higher score in Innovation & AI Application, then Problem Identification & Trader Relevance, then Technical Feasibility. Round 2 - On-Campus Hackathon at IIT Bombay The top 50 teams develop their proposed innovations into working prototypes and demonstrate them at Techfest, IIT Bombay. Detailed format and judging guidelines will be shared with shortlisted teams. Timeline Registration closes - 30th November 2026 Round 1 submission deadline - 30th November 2026 Shortlist announcement - 5th December 2026 Finals (on-campus hackathon at IIT Bombay) - 15th-18th December 2026 Rewards and Prizes INR 50,000 for the top 3 winners. Certificates for all participants who qualify for Round 2.

A Chance to Share and Build Ideas Health Hackathon 3.0 invites innovators, students, and researchers to present their concepts and refine them further. The emphasis is on practical, high-impact solutions designed to reach underserved communities and individuals facing healthcare access barriers. Event Overview & Key Dates • Pre-Event Workshop: 27 January 2027 • Main Hackathon: 28 & 29 January 2027 • Venue: VIT Bhopal University, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh • Total Prize Pool: ₹2 Lakh     Registration & Submission Registration is now open. title: Rewired (Tech Hackathon)
description: Note: This Event is happening in Bangalore! Event Description: Rewired is a build-and-pitch hackathon. Teams pick a real problem from this year's theme, turn it into a working prototype in 7 hours and pitch it to a jury. It rewards problem sharpness, sound execution, original thinking and the ability to explain why the idea matters to a real user. Coders, designers and business minds are all welcome. Theme: The Invisible City Every city runs on things nobody sees: voices no system understands, people who keep everything working but never appear in any database, waste nobody counts, and needs nobody says out loud. Find something real that the city overlooks, and build technology that makes it heard, seen, counted or said. Event Design: Team size: 2 to 4 members. Eligibility: Open to currently enrolled students from any college or university with a valid college ID. Teams may be cross-college. One person, one team. Equipment: Participants must bring their own laptops, chargers, an extension board and any hardware they use. Power at every desk, Wi-Fi, meals and water are provided at the venue. The Gravity Well: At the start of the Offline Round, each team chooses 1 out of 2 envelopes. It reveals a real-world constraint that the team has to build around.  Tools: Any language, framework, platform, API, library or AI tool may be used, provided it is declared. Competition Rounds: Online Round Topic: Restaurants, bakeries, supermarkets and households regularly have surplus food, while people nearby may struggle to afford meals. The challenge is often coordination, timing and safe distribution. Solve this challenge and submit the deliverables listed below for the online round selections.  Challenge: Bridge the gap between those with excess food and those without access to it.  Deliverable: One Concept Brief PDF of up to 2 pages (team, problem with real evidence, target user, proposed solution, tech approach, expected impact, and a 12-hour build plan) and one pitch video of up to 2 minutes in which at least two members appear and speak.  Language: English or Hindi. Videos must have subtitles in English or Hindi. Format: PDF for the brief. .mp4, .mpeg, .avi or .mov for the video. Submission: Upload the brief and video to a Google Drive folder named "Rewired_Team_Name_MWRTMB" set to "Anyone with the link can view", and submit the Drive link, repository link and Orbit. Inaccessible link:   If the link cannot be opened at the time of judging, it will be at the discretion of the OC whether the submission will be considered or not. Shortlisting: The Top 20 teams move to the Offline Round. Offline Round – 19 November 2026 Duration: Exactly 7 hours of build time, from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM. The clock runs through meals and check-ins. Build window: All code, design and assets must be created inside the build window. Push the tags checkpoint-1 by 11:30 AM, checkpoint-2 by 2:30 PM and final by 5:00 PM. GitHub's server push times are the official record. Checkpoints: Each team is assigned one mentor for the day, who holds two check-ins of about 20 minutes during the build. Checkpoints are not scored. Problem Case: A new problem case will be presented to the team at the venue on the day of the offline round.  Submission: Before 5:00 PM, submit the repository link and final commit, a demo link, a mandatory demo video of up to 2 minutes and a completed README through the Google Form provided at the start. Name the Drive folder "REWIRED_TeamID_MWRTMB" and set links to "Anyone with the link can view". Event Horizon Crossing: At 5:00 PM code is frozen. No pushes, Drive changes or redeployments after this point. The recorded final commit is what is judged. Final pitch: All teams pitch to one of four judging panels for 5 minutes, followed by 3 minutes of Q&A. The top teams from each panel go to the Final Orbit and pitch again to the Grand Jury for the top two places. Declarations: Declare all open-source libraries, templates, APIs, datasets and AI tools used, and confirm that the project was built by your team inside the build window through the google form that will be shared at the start. Rules: Original work: The project must be built by the team inside the build window. Pre-existing projects, old code and borrowed products are not allowed. Open-source libraries, public APIs, templates, UI kits and official project generators are allowed if declared. AI: AI-assisted tools are allowed if declared. Any judge may ask any member to explain any part of the project. If a team cannot explain a core part, its Technical execution score is capped at 10/25. Prototype: Slide-only submissions are not allowed. A working prototype, even a partial one, is required for the Offline Round. If a live demo fails, the team may use its demo video within its pitch time. Team changes: Team members cannot be changed after the Online Round closes. A shortlisted team may replace or drop one member only with written OC approval. Data and IP: Teams must not use confidential or scraped personal data. Teams retain the IP of what they build. Milkyway may feature submissions for promotion with credit to the team.  Pitch time: Pitches over 5 minutes will be cut off by the timekeeper. Conduct: Teams must follow the Code of Conduct and venue rules. Any harassment, sabotage, interference with another team or misuse of the network leads to immediate disqualification. Penalties: All violations will be dealt with under the General Rules, at the discretion of the OC, as set out in the "Penalties and Disqualification" section. Any other consequences will be taken at the discretion of the OC. Any changes to these rules will be informed to the participants prior to the event. Prizes: Results will be announced on stage and through mails to all the Participants. 1st place: ₹12,000 and direct entry to the Milkyway Finale. 2nd place: ₹8,000. Note: Participants shall refer to the General Rules and the Event Horizon Official Participant Rulebook for further details.

title: Seed Hackathon 2026
description: SEED Hackathon 2026 The Age of Autonomy A chance to build something that matters. Event Overview: Format: Virtual | Free to Participate Event Dates: 10 October  – 9 December 2026 Grand Finale: 9 December 2026 Team Size: 2–3 Members Cash Prize Pool: ₹2,00,000 University Partners: Boston University & GW Engineering Who Can Participate? Whether you're a student exploring technology or a professional already working in the field, this is your chance to put your skills to the test! Eligibility: Final Year & Pre-Final Year Students from BE / BTech / BSc / BCA backgrounds First Year & Second Year Students from ME / MTech / MSc / MCA backgrounds Working Professionals in Technical Roles What's the Hackathon About? What happens when AI starts making decisions on its own? That's the big question behind SEED Hackathon 2026. Organised in collaboration with Boston University and GW Engineering , this global virtual hackathon brings together curious minds to tackle real-world challenges in AI and automation! You'll work with your team to turn an idea into a working prototype, learn from industry experts, and showcase your skills on a global platform. Three Unqiue Challenges: Choose a challenge that excites you and build a solution that makes a difference. No Screens: Explore smarter ways to interact with technology without traditional screens. Chain of Command: Build AI agents that collaborate and solve problems together. The Kill Switch: Design AI systems that are safer, more accountable, and easier to control. What's in It for You? Beyond building something exciting, there's plenty to take away. ₹2,00,000 in Cash Prizes 1st Place: ₹50,000 per team 2nd Place: ₹35,000 per team 3rd Place: ₹15,000 per team Two winning teams will be selected for each position. And that's not all! Up to 75% tuition scholarships at partner universities Application fee waivers for placing teams Expert mentorship and hands-on learning Recognition from leading global universities Participation certificates and networking opportunities Important Dates: Here's your roadmap from idea to finale. 10 October: Registrations & Abstract Submissions Open 22 November: Abstract Submission Deadline 24 November: Shortlist Announcement 25 November – 2 December: Build Your Prototype 3–7 December: Expert Mentorship 9 December: Grand Finale Your First Step: Submit an Abstract Have an idea? Tell us about it! An abstract is simply a short summary of what you want to build. You don't need a finished product to get started. Just tell us: The Problem: What are you trying to solve? Your Solution: How do you plan to tackle it? The Impact: Why does your idea matter? Maximum Length: 1,000 words Submission Deadline: 22 November 2026 Shortlisted teams will move on to the prototyping phase, where they'll bring their ideas to life with expert support. Ready to Build the Future? You bring the ideas. We'll bring the platform, the mentorship, and the opportunity to make them real. Register, explore the challenges, and submit your abstract here: https://seedglobal.io/vtddw72os

title: CODERED'26
description: CODERED ’26 - National-Level Product Development Challenge CODERED ’26, organised by the Entrepreneurship Cell of BMS Institute of Technology and Management, Bengaluru, is a national-level product development challenge designed to take student teams beyond conventional hackathons and enable them to build meaningful, functional products. Unlike traditional hackathons that revolve around solving predefined problem statements within a limited timeframe, CODERED ’26 follows a comprehensive product development journey, from ideation and conceptualisation to development, testing and validation. This edition brings together six participating companies, offering students the opportunity to work on real-world product ideas across multiple domains.  Check out our WEBSITE for the Challenge Briefs. https://codered26.xyz Company Tracks: CODERED ’26 features four tracks, with six participating companies: Dedicated Company Tracks: Niveus Technologies Simple Energy Agnes AI XP Robotis Unisys (for BMSIT Students Only) Each of these companies will have a dedicated track featuring one or more product ideas for participating teams. Startup Track: The Startup Track brings together product opportunities from: Think Robotics Sahasranshu Technologies MyStartupWave Cassette Labs The participating companies may provide multiple product ideas within their respective domains. Teams can explore the available ideas and select one product idea from one company to work on throughout the competition. Teams are not required to work on every idea offered under a track. Refer the BROCHURE for more information Eligibility and Team Composition: The eligibility criteria, team composition requirements and inter-college/inter-specialisation participation guidelines will remain the same as those followed in the previous edition of CODERED. Participants are required to adhere to the team formation and eligibility conditions specified during registration. Registration and Participation Guidelines: Teams must complete the registration process through the official Unstop opportunity page. Participants must submit their ideas in the prescribed format within the stipulated deadline. Each team may select only one product idea from one participating company. Teams must continue working on the product idea selected during the competition. Teams are expected to develop their ideas into functional prototypes or MVPs during the product development journey. All participants must comply with the competition guidelines and instructions issued by the organisers. The CODERED ’26 Experience: CODERED ’26 aims to provide students with an opportunity to experience the complete product development process while engaging with industry and emerging companies. Through company-led product opportunities, structured evaluation rounds and an intensive offline development sprint, participants will get the opportunity to move beyond theoretical ideas and work towards building functional products. title: Defy'27

The hackathon follows a two-round format, beginning with an online idea submission round, followed by an intensive 24-hour onsite hackathon at VIT Chennai for shortlisted teams. Dates are tentative and may be updated. Any changes will be announced on the official platform. Tracks DeFi Public goods Open innovation Teams choose one track and identify their own problem statement within it. Prizes DeFy'27 offers a total prize pool of ₹1,00,000 . We will announce the detailed prize distribution soon. Round 1: Online Idea Submission Step 1: Choose a Track Explore the three tracks and select the one that best aligns with your interests and the problem you wish to address. Step 2: Identify a Problem Statement Identify a meaningful real-world problem within your chosen track. Understand the problem, its target audience and the opportunity for an innovative solution. Step 3: Form Your Team Create a team of 4 to 6 members on the official hackathon registration platform. Ensure all members join the team and complete the registration process. Step 4: Develop Your Idea Develop an innovative solution aligned with your selected track. Your proposal should demonstrate the potential to become a practical, Web3-powered solution. Think beyond technology. Consider your business model, target audience, feasibility, scalability and real-world impact. Step 5: Submit Your Idea Complete the prescribed submission template and provide all the required details. Your submission must clearly outline: The problem you aim to solve. Your proposed solution. Its alignment with your selected track. How Web3 contributes to your solution. Its potential business value and real-world impact. Step 6: Shortlisting Results All submissions will be evaluated based on innovation, relevance, feasibility and potential impact. The most promising teams will be shortlisted for Round 2 and notified about their qualification for the onsite hackathon. Round 2: Onsite Hackathon (9-10 January 2027) Step 7: Confirm Your Participation Shortlisted teams must complete the required RSVP process to confirm their participation in the onsite hackathon. Step 8: The 24-Hour Hackathon Qualified teams will participate in an intensive, in-person 24-hour hackathon at VIT Chennai, starting on 9 January and concluding on 10 January 2027. Step 9: Build Your Submitted Project Teams must develop the project proposed during Round 1. The final project must remain aligned with the original submission and selected track. Participants are expected to transform their initial ideas into working solutions, demonstrating technical execution, innovation and entrepreneurial thinking. Important Reminders Teams must have 4 to 6 members . Choose one of the 3 tracks that aligns with your interests and proposed solution. Ensure your problem statement and solution fit your selected track. Complete team formation and registration as instructed. Submit your idea using the prescribed template. Await the Round 1 shortlisting results. Shortlisted teams must complete their RSVP and attend the onsite hackathon on 9-10 January 2027. The project developed during Round 2 must correspond to the original Round 1 submission. Identify a problem. Develop an idea. Build your solution. Bring your vision to life at DeFy'27! Organised by DAO Community and Business Innovation Community VIT Chennai.

title: IDEATHON- FutureX: Innovating for Global Challenges
description: FUTUREX 2026 – Innovating for Global Challenges What if your idea could help solve a real-world problem and contribute to a better future? Skill2Career, Ed-Tech platform presents FutureX 2026 , an innovation-driven Ideathon that brings together students to identify global challenges, think beyond conventional solutions, and propose innovative ideas that create meaningful impact. title: LightHouse - Hackathon
description: About LightHouse: LightHouse is an international, online hackathon for builders of agentic AI. Over several weeks, teams design and ship autonomous AI agents that plan, reason, use tools, and take action to solve real-world problems. Whether you’re a student, a developer, or an early-stage founder, this is your chance to build, get noticed, and win. Mandatory for Registration: Registration is complete only when all team members do of the following: Fill the Profile Review Form: https://tally.so/r/1Wd0MM Prizes: ₹10,000 in cash prizes ₹5,00,000 in kind (credits, tools, mentorship, perks, and opportunities from partners) Eligibility: Open to participants worldwide (students, professionals, and independent builders). Team size: 2 to 5 members. Inter-college and inter-specialization teams are allowed. Each participant can be part of only one team. Basic knowledge of programming and AI/LLM concepts is recommended. Format: Fully online, with no travel required. Teams work on one problem statement from the released set and build an agentic AI solution. Timeline: Stage Dates Registration 13 Nov – 25 Dec Round 1: Profile Review 15 Nov – 1 Dec Problem Statements Released 1 Dec (announcements continue until 30 Dec) Round 2: Build Phase (working on the problem statement) 1 Jan – 10 Jan Final Submission 11 Jan Grand Finale Online (date and time to be announced) Process: Register your team before the deadline. Your team’s profiles go through a profile review. Shortlisted teams receive the problem statements. Pick one problem statement and build your agentic AI solution from 1 to 10 Jan. Submit your project on 11 Jan (working demo, GitHub repository, demo video, and a short write-up). Top teams present live at the online finale in front of judges. Rules: All work must be created during the build phase; pre-existing code is allowed only if it is open-source and disclosed. Solutions must use an agentic AI approach (autonomous planning, tool use, or multi-step reasoning). Plagiarism or copied projects lead to disqualification. Any AI models, APIs, and frameworks are allowed, but you must credit them. Teams must submit before the deadline. Late submissions won’t be considered. The organisers’ and judges’ decisions are final. Follow the code of conduct and behave respectfully with other participants. Judging Criteria: Innovation, agentic capability and autonomy, technical depth, real-world impact, usability, and presentation.
